summary: Rockwell Light, an octagonal tower on Bray's Point at the Fox River mouth in Oshkosh, built by a private owner in 1909-10 and relit in 1986.

light.note: Fixed red. Focal height 26 ft (7.9 m) above low water per LighthouseFriends; the Lighthouse Directory gives about 49 ft (15 m). The record's 15.0 m is not confirmed by LighthouseFriends.

structures.note: Built 1910 per LighthouseFriends and the Lighthouse Directory; 1909 per IPL and Penberthy. Material disputed: concrete (LighthouseFriends) or brick (Lighthouse Directory). 42 ft (13 m) tall.

staffing.note: Privately operated. Light Lists name operators from the 1920s to at least 1965; no resident keeper after 1917 is named in the sources read.

access.note: Privately owned. Grounds and tower closed. Can be seen from the street at the corner of Lake Street and Bay Shore Drive.

visit.note: Grounds and tower closed; the lighthouse can be seen and photographed from the street.

events.note: Plans drawn in 1909 by George A. Rockwell, who died before the work was finished. IPL and Penberthy give 1909 as the year it was built.
Completed in 1910 at William Bray's expense (LighthouseFriends; Lighthouse Directory).
Lit as a private light after completion in 1910 (LighthouseFriends; Lighthouse Directory).
Point sold to Harry C. Stutz (LighthouseFriends).
Title passed through Frank H. Wheeler; John C. Thompson, an Oshkosh attorney, bought the point (LighthouseFriends).
Thompson remodeled the house on the point and restored the lighthouse (LighthouseFriends).
Restored and relit by new owners (Lighthouse Directory; IPL; Penberthy).

keepers.name: William Bray
keepers.note: Private owner who had the light built. Penberthy says he took on the keeper's work and lit the lamp each night. Not a government keeper.

keepers.name: Mrs. Thompson
keepers.note: Appointed keeper per IPL, when the light was called Thompson's Point Lighthouse. First name not given. IPL does not say which Thompson she was. LighthouseFriends does not mention a keeper in 1917.

keepers.name: John C. Thompson
keepers.note: Listed as operator of the light in the Light Lists (LighthouseFriends). Bought the point in 1918.

keepers.name: A.J. Coffey
keepers.note: Superintendent of the Cook & Brown Lime Company; listed as responsible for the light (LighthouseFriends).

keepers.name: John Buckstaff
keepers.note: Listed as operator from 1948 until at least 1965; purchased the property in the mid-1940s (LighthouseFriends). Named only in his role as operator and owner.

corrections.why: LighthouseFriends says the lighthouse is privately owned; the Lighthouse Directory says privately maintained.

LighthouseFriends gives 26 ft (7.9 m) above low water, and Wikipedia repeats that figure from LighthouseFriends. The Lighthouse Directory gives about 49 ft (15 m) focal plane, which may be the source of the record's 15.0. Needs a human decision.

The Lighthouse Directory, IPL and Penberthy all place the light going dark in the 1950s. LighthouseFriends says the operator was listed until at least 1965, which does not date the light going dark. The record's 1965 is not supported as the deactivation year.

The Lighthouse Directory lists it as active and privately maintained, and IPL's 2020 copy says it continues to show a fixed red light. LighthouseFriends says it no longer appears on the Coast Guard Light List. A human should check the present state before this changes.

notes_for_editor: No USLHS roster: the USLHS place search for the Oshkosh light found no matching station (the nearest entry, Rockwell Memorial, is a minor aid with no roster and no position match). The keepers here come from LighthouseFriends, Penberthy and IPL, not from NARA registers. Mrs. Thompson (1917) rests on IPL alone and conflicts with LighthouseFriends, which dates John C. Thompson's purchase to 1918 after Stutz and Wheeler; a Light List for 1917-1918 would settle it, and none is in the local corpus. The corpus search for Rockwell, Bray's Point, Thompson's Point and Oshkosh in the Lighthouse Board, Commissioner and Bulletin series found nothing about this light. Chronicling America returned no Oshkosh page on the light in two searches. The Oshkosh Daily Northwestern article of 21 April 1961 that LighthouseFriends cites was not available to read. The SAH Archipedia entry returned 403 and was not read. Wikipedia was used only for leads (its infobox matches the sources above; its government-costs sentence is not cited here). The 1885 Fox River rescue by Otto B. Storbeck (Life-Saving Service medal) is unconnected to this light and is left out. John Buckstaff's public role as operator and buyer is named; family details from LighthouseFriends are left out because he may be living. Photos: the record's Wikimedia image has no licence and was not checked, so none is listed.
